record.name: Grenada
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. The digital transformation minister's portfolio explicitly includes AI policy across sectors.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. The retrieved material does not sufficiently establish the national AI governance arrangements. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

Re-ran searches in English for a government-designated institute that evaluates advanced models, or a commitment, proposal or study naming one. No qualifying institute or commitment was identified; results described the June 2026 appointment of a Minister for Digital Transformation with an AI policy portfolio and the digital transformation agenda. Retrieved the Government Gazette as new primary governance evidence. Raised confidence to medium under the status-confidence rule: recorded queries in English and a national or official language, and cited primary governance evidence consistent with no qualifying institute. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Checked the Government Gazette after the 5 November 2026 general election, up to No. 57 of 6 November 2026: no new assignment of AI policy and no commencement notice for the Digital Transformation Agency Act. Partial check; the last full-check date is unchanged.

check.language_note: English is an official language or an official language of national administration; it is a practical national search language for this check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. On 24 October 2026 the record was searched again in English; the result links of each query were matched against registered sources in the same way.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: The CTU table records national AI-strategy and readiness-assessment status; its country row does not substantively corroborate institute status or establish independence from national reporting. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence.
check.governance_note: The Government Gazette of 5 June 2026 designates a Minister for Digital Transformation whose responsibilities include AI policy, embedded across sectors as part of the digital transformation framework, alongside cybersecurity. It assigns no body the evaluation of advanced models.

record.notes: The Cabinet Office ICT division page lists 'AI-Powered Government Tools' among its services. The minister for digital transformation appointed in June 2026 has AI policy in his portfolio (Government Gazette No. 26 of 2026; NOW Grenada). The Digital Transformation Agency Act 2026 (Act No. 10 of 2026, assented on 31 August 2026) establishes an agency to lead, coordinate and oversee digital transformation across the public sector, and lets it audit public bodies' operations against the Government's digital transformation initiatives; no provision names artificial intelligence. It comes into operation on a day the minister appoints by notice in the Gazette. The CTU report (July 2026) lists 'None reported' for a national AI strategy. This is an absence of findings.

next_check.reason: Look for the post-election assignment of AI policy and digital transformation in the Government Gazette.
